detailHeading: Why woodwork moves in Georgian Bay homes
detailBody: Wood swells in humid summers and shrinks when the furnace runs all winter. Around Collingwood and Nottawasaga Bay, the swing is wide. Doors start to stick, mitred trim joints open, and caulk lines crack at the corners.

Exterior wood takes the most abuse. Window sills, door thresholds and deck boards sit wet through spring melt and freeze-thaw cycles. Soft spots, peeling paint and dark stains are early signs of rot. Catching rot early keeps the repair small, often a sill or a few boards instead of the framing below.

Older homes and cottages bring their own quirks. Walls are rarely square and floors are rarely level. Trim often needs scribing and shimming to fit, and matching the existing profile helps a repair blend with the rest of the room. Mention the age of the home in your request.

faqs.q: Will new trim match my existing woodwork?
faqs.a: Matching depends on the profile, size and wood species. Older or custom profiles are harder to find. Include a close-up photo of the existing trim, and the service provider can talk through options, such as replacing the trim on a full wall for a consistent look.

faqs.q: Can the request include paint or stain?
faqs.a: Yes. Mention whether you want new woodwork filled, sanded and finished with paint or stain. The service provider can confirm whether finishing fits the same request.

faqs.q: How is rot repair handled?
faqs.a: Rot repair usually means removing soft wood back to solid material and replacing the damaged section. Finding the water source, such as missing flashing or a failed caulk joint, helps stop the rot from returning. Include photos of the stained or soft areas.

faqs.q: What about damaged framing or subfloor?
faqs.a: Describe any soft floors, sagging or damaged joists in your request. Structural work may need a permit or a licensed contractor in Ontario, and the service provider can confirm what applies.

faqs.q: Are small carpentry jobs worth a request?
faqs.a: Yes. A single sticking door, a cracked casing or one loose stair railing is worth a request. List several small items together so the service provider can review them as one job.

detailBody: Caulk is the first line of defence at every tub and shower joint. Watch for black spots under the surface, edges lifting away from the tile, gaps at the corners and soft grout nearby. Mould under the bead usually means water has already worked behind the seal.

Fresh caulk over old caulk rarely lasts. The new bead bonds to the failing one, not to the tile or tub. A lasting job starts with full removal of the old material and a clean, dry joint, then a mould-resistant silicone in one continuous bead.

Cottage bathrooms see extra stress. A cold, closed building over winter and a humid, busy summer make joints expand and shrink. A spring check of the caulk lines before the first guests arrive catches small gaps early.

faqs.q: How do you know when caulk needs replacing?
faqs.a: Look for cracks, peeling edges, gaps at the corners or mould you cannot wipe away. If water sits in the joint or the bead feels soft, the seal has failed. Replacing failing caulk early protects the subfloor and wall framing.

faqs.q: Why not caulk over the old bead?
faqs.a: New caulk does not bond well to old caulk, soap film or mould. The fresh bead peels away and traps moisture behind the seal. Full removal and a clean, dry surface give the new caulk a proper bond.

faqs.q: When is the shower ready to use again?
faqs.a: Silicone needs time to cure before water touches the joint. The cure time on the product label sets the wait. Plan for the tub or shower to stay out of use until then.

faqs.q: What if there is water damage behind the caulk?
faqs.a: Mention any soft drywall, loose tile or stains on the ceiling below in your request. The service provider can confirm what the repair involves. Work on supply or drain lines may need a licensed plumber in Ontario, and the service provider can confirm what applies.

faqs.q: Do I need to do anything to prepare?
faqs.a: Clear bottles, mats and shower caddies from the area. Avoid running the tub or shower right before the visit so the joints start dry.

detailHeading: What makes tile last in a Collingwood home
detailBody: Most tile failures start below the tile. A floor with too much bounce cracks grout lines. A shower wall without a waterproof membrane lets water into the framing. Checking the subfloor and walls first shows whether backer board, membrane or levelling is needed.

Entryways and mudrooms take hard wear in this area. Beach sand in summer and road salt and slush in winter grind at grout. A durable floor tile, a sealed or stain-resistant grout and a good mat at the door all help.
Layout matters as much as materials. Good reference lines put the cuts at the edges of the room, not in the middle of the floor, and line the pattern up with doors and counters.

faqs.q: Can the request use tile I already bought?
faqs.a: Yes. Mention the tile you already have. Check the boxes share the same lot number and keep extra for cuts and future repairs. The service provider can confirm the setting materials and trim pieces the job needs.

faqs.q: Do I need backer board or a membrane?
faqs.a: Wet areas such as shower walls and tub surrounds need a waterproof membrane or a waterproof backer system. Floors need a flat, stiff base. Photos of the existing surface help the service provider confirm what your space needs.

faqs.q: Is matching existing tile possible for a repair?
faqs.a: Often, if you kept spare tiles from the original job. If not, look for a close match and include a photo with your request. For a consistent look, some homeowners replace a full area, such as a backsplash wall, instead of a few tiles.

faqs.q: How do I care for new tile?
faqs.a: Wipe up spills and clean with a pH-neutral cleaner. Reseal cement grout on the schedule the grout maker recommends, especially in showers. Keep a mat at entry doors to catch sand and salt before they reach the tile.

faqs.q: Are cottage bathrooms and entryways covered?
faqs.a: Yes. Requests for homes and cottages are both welcome. Cottage floors deal with sand, wet feet and an unheated winter, so tile and grout suited to seasonal use are worth discussing.

detailHeading: Choosing the height and wall for your TV
detailBody: The most common mistake is mounting a TV too high. For seated viewing, the centre of the screen sits best close to eye level from the couch. Above a fireplace, a tilting or pull-down mount brings the picture back toward a comfortable angle.

The wall matters as much as the mount. Drywall needs studs or added blocking. Plaster walls in older homes crack without careful drilling. Brick, stone and log walls in cottages need anchors suited to masonry or solid wood. Mention the wall type in your request.

Plan the cables before the mount goes up. Low-voltage HDMI and network cables run inside the wall with the right kit. A new power outlet behind the TV is electrical work, so a licensed electrician may be required. The service provider can confirm what applies.

faqs.q: What size TVs can be mounted?
faqs.a: Most flat-screen sizes, from a small bedroom TV to a large living room screen. The limit comes from the mount rating and the wall. Include the TV model in your request so the hardware suits the weight.

faqs.q: Do I need to supply the mount?
faqs.a: Either way works. Buy a mount rated for your TV’s size and weight, or ask the service provider about a fixed, tilting or full-motion style for the room. Have the TV’s model number ready so the mount pattern matches.

faqs.q: Will the cables be hidden?
faqs.a: Cords are hidden with a paintable raceway on the wall or routed inside the wall with a low-voltage kit. Where the job needs a new outlet behind the TV, a licensed electrician may be required, and the service provider can confirm what applies.

faqs.q: Can a TV go on brick, stone or plaster?
faqs.a: Yes. Each wall type needs different anchors and drilling. Mention the wall material and include a photo so the service provider can confirm suitable fasteners.

faqs.q: Can a TV be mounted outdoors?
faqs.a: Often, on covered porches and patios. Outdoor setups need a weather-rated mount and a TV made for outdoor use or kept under good cover. A new exterior outlet needs a licensed electrician.

detailBody: Preparation decides how long paint lasts. Filling holes, sanding rough patches, cleaning greasy or dusty surfaces and spot-priming repairs all come before the finish coats. Skipping this step shows up as peeling, uneven sheen or patches visible through the new colour.

Bathrooms and cottage kitchens see heavy humidity. A mould-resistant paint in a satin or semi-gloss sheen holds up better than flat paint in these rooms, and a working exhaust fan matters as much as the paint. Mention the room and how it is used in your request.

Exterior painting depends on the weather. Paint needs dry surfaces and temperatures within the range on the label, so most exterior work around Collingwood happens from late spring to early fall. Walls facing south and west take the most sun and fade first.

faqs.q: Do I need to move my furniture?
faqs.a: Move small items, art and breakables before the visit. Mention anything large, fragile or heavy in your request so the service provider can plan for it.

faqs.q: When is the best time for exterior painting?
faqs.a: Late spring to early fall brings the dry days and temperatures exterior paint needs. Surfaces must be dry, and cool, damp nights near the water slow drying. Send your request early in the year to plan around the weather.

faqs.q: Will touch-ups match my existing colour?
faqs.a: Keep leftover paint or the colour name if you have them. A paint store matches a colour from a small chip too. Touch-ups on older paint sometimes show, so repainting a full wall often gives a more even look.

faqs.q: Are kitchen cabinets covered?

detailHeading: Keeping rental properties in good repair
detailBody: Small repairs left too long turn into bigger ones. A failed caulk line becomes a soft subfloor. A loose railing becomes a safety issue. Regular checks and steady attention to tenant reports keep units in good shape.

Turnovers are the best time to catch up. With the unit empty, walls get patched and painted, doors and trim fixed, tubs and sinks re-caulked, and smoke and carbon monoxide alarms checked before the next tenant moves in. Photos of finished items go into your records.

Rental cottages and seasonal units around Georgian Bay add more work. Opening and closing, storm checks and freeze protection fit into the same maintenance plan. Work needing a licensed plumber, electrician or gas technician is a separate trade, and the service provider can confirm what applies.

faqs.q: Can visits be coordinated with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes, if you want. Share your rules on notice, entry and communication in your request so visits follow your process and you stay informed.

faqs.q: Are turnover make-readies covered?
faqs.a: Yes. A turnover punch list often covers patching, painting, caulking, door and trim repairs and alarm checks. Photos of finished items help with your listing and move-in condition records.

faqs.q: Can one request cover several properties?
faqs.a: Yes. Requests for single units and for several properties are both welcome. Share your locations and the work you send out most, and the service provider can suggest a way to group visits.

faqs.q: How are jobs quoted?

detailBody: A cottage left empty for months around Georgian Bay faces freeze-thaw cycles, heavy snow loads, wind off the bay and mice looking for a warm spot. Most damage starts small, such as a lifted shingle or a gap under a door, and grows when nobody is there to notice.

Regular checks catch these problems early. A walk-through on the schedule you choose looks for water, pests, storm damage and security issues, with photos so you see the cottage without making the drive.

faqs.q: How often should my cottage be checked in winter?

detailBody: Winter around Georgian Bay is hard on a closed cottage. Ice and snow lift shingles and push on decks. Water left in a line or fitting freezes and cracks the pipe, and the leak only shows once the water is back on. Mice move in through small gaps and chew insulation.

A careful opening checks the building before water goes back into the lines. That means a walk around the exterior, an interior inspection and a watch on fixtures and visible pipes for leaks as the system fills. Start-up of a well pump, pressure tank, water heater or any gas appliance needs a licensed plumber or gas technician.
Owners who are away share access details, such as a lockbox code, and a contact for decisions. Many owners aim to open before the Victoria Day long weekend, so send your request early in spring.

faqs.q: When should I book my cottage opening?
faqs.a: Send your request early in spring, especially if you plan to arrive for the Victoria Day long weekend. Weather and access, such as road conditions and lingering snow on the property, affect timing.

faqs.q: Is turning the water back on covered?
faqs.a: Opening fixtures and watching for leaks as water returns is part of a typical opening. Starting a well pump or pressure tank, and starting gas appliances such as a water heater or furnace, needs a licensed plumber or gas technician.

faqs.q: What if the opening finds a problem?
faqs.a: Ask to be contacted with photos and a description before any repair goes ahead. Handyman repairs, such as a damaged step or failed caulk, can be added to the quote. Cracked pipes and gas issues go to a licensed trade.

faqs.q: Do I need to be there?
faqs.a: No. Owners who are away share access details, such as a lockbox code or key arrangement, and a phone number for decisions. Ask for photos and notes once the opening checks are done.

faqs.q: Is cottage closing covered too?

seoTitle: Cottage Closing in Collingwood | Collingwood Handyman
seoDescription: Request a quote for cottage closing around Collingwood and Georgian Bay. Describe draining lines, sealing gaps and securing the cottage. Call 705-795-4009.
h1: Cottage closing to protect your property over winter.
sub: Request a quote to drain water lines, seal entry points and secure your cottage for winter. Well and gas shutdowns need a licensed trade.
cardsIntro: Send a cottage closing request for Collingwood, Wasaga Beach or Oro-Medonte, so the property is ready for freezing weather before you head home.

cards.title: Water drain-down
cards.body: Supply shut off, taps opened, lines drained and plumbing antifreeze added to traps and toilets to protect against freezing.

cards.title: Well & gas shutdown
cards.body: Well pump, pressure tank, water heater and gas appliance shutdowns need a licensed plumber or gas technician.

cards.title: Pest prevention
cards.body: Small gaps sealed, food removed, the fridge propped open and the spots mice use to get inside over winter closed up.

cards.title: Secure & document
cards.body: Outdoor furniture stored, every door and window lock checked, and photos taken so you have a record of the cottage’s condition.

scopeNote: Well, water heater and gas appliance shutdown in Ontario needs a licensed contractor or gas technician, and the service provider can confirm what applies.
processHeading: From last weekend to locked up for winter.

steps.title: Describe the job
steps.body: Share the location, the water and heat systems, and when you plan to leave for the season.

steps.title: A service provider reviews it
steps.body: A local service provider reviews the request and confirms coverage for your cottage.

steps.title: Talk through scope and next steps
steps.body: Go over the closing tasks, any well or gas trade work, access details and whether you want winter checks.

detailHeading: Why a careful closing matters on Georgian Bay
detailBody: Water left in a pipe, trap or fixture expands when frozen and cracks the fitting. The leak stays hidden until spring, when the water goes back on. A careful drain-down and plumbing antifreeze in every trap and toilet protect the system through the coldest months.

Closing also means keeping animals and weather out. Mice look for warm, quiet buildings in the fall. Sealing small gaps, removing food and other attractants, and storing outdoor furniture and cushions before snow arrives all help.

Owners who are away share access details and a contact for decisions. Shutdown of a well pump, pressure tank, water heater or gas appliance needs a licensed plumber or gas technician. Ask about winter checks if your insurer requires visits to a vacant cottage.

faqs.q: When should I close my cottage?
faqs.a: Close before the first hard frost, once you are done with the season. Waiting too long risks a cold snap before the lines are drained. Send your request early in the fall, since many owners close around the same weekends.

faqs.q: Is the water heater part of the closing?
faqs.a: Yes, the water heater belongs in the closing plan. Draining or shutting down a gas water heater, along with any other gas appliance, needs a licensed gas technician. The service provider can confirm who handles each step.

faqs.q: What happens if the lines are not drained properly?
faqs.a: Water left in a line or fitting freezes, expands and cracks the pipe. The damage often stays hidden until spring, when the water goes back on and the leak soaks floors, walls or cabinets.

faqs.q: Should I leave some heat on?
faqs.a: Some owners keep low heat on all winter, others shut the heat off and fully drain the system. The right choice depends on the building and your insurance. The service provider can talk through both, and furnace or gas work goes to a licensed technician.

faqs.q: Are winter checks available after closing?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask about property checks through the off-season, with photos after each visit. See the cottage maintenance page for what a check covers, or ask about combining closing, winter checks and spring opening.

sub: Describe the repairs, safety checks and photos your unit needs between tenants, and request a quote to get it ready to show and ready for move-in.
cardsHeading: Get the unit ready for the next tenant.
cardsIntro: Send a request to prepare a rental unit in Collingwood, Wasaga Beach or Stayner, for landlords and property managers.

cards.title: Pre-listing walk-through
cards.body: A walk through the unit with you, or on your behalf, to build a punch list of repairs, touch-ups and safety items.

cards.title: Turnover repairs
cards.body: Drywall patches, paint touch-ups, trim and flooring fixes, and tub and counter re-caulking before the unit is listed.

cards.title: Locks & alarms
cards.body: Locks re-keyed or replaced between tenants, and smoke and carbon monoxide alarms tested, with battery units replaced where needed.

cards.title: Photos & access
cards.body: Before-and-after photos for your listing and move-in records, and help coordinating access for showings with you or your leasing agent.

scopeNote: Work needing a licensed plumber or electrician in Ontario is a separate trade, and the service provider can confirm what applies.
processHeading: From empty unit to move-in ready.

steps.title: Describe the job
steps.body: Share the address, the move-out date and any repairs or concerns you have noted.

steps.title: A service provider reviews it
steps.body: A local service provider reviews the request and confirms coverage for the unit.

steps.title: Talk through scope and next steps
steps.body: Go over the punch list, access and any trade requirements before work begins.

detailHeading: What the request covers, and what stays with the landlord
detailBody: Tenant placement has two sides. One is the physical unit: repairs, paint, locks, alarms and a clean, documented handover. The other is finding and signing the tenant. This request covers the first part only.

Tenant screening, leases and legal advice are not part of this request. Landlords should follow the Ontario Residential Tenancies Act and use the Ontario standard lease form. Questions about screening, rent or tenant rights belong with a lawyer, a paralegal or the Landlord and Tenant Board.

A well-prepared unit helps on both sides. Clear photos support your listing, and a documented move-in condition gives you and the tenant a shared record. Work needing a licensed plumber or electrician is a separate trade, and the service provider can confirm what applies.

faqs.q: Does this include tenant screening or leases?
faqs.a: No. The request covers preparing the unit. The landlord or property manager handles screening, the lease and the tenancy. Follow the Ontario Residential Tenancies Act and use the Ontario standard lease form. For legal questions, speak with a lawyer or paralegal.

faqs.q: Can access for showings be coordinated?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Describe your access setup with you or your leasing agent, such as a lockbox, so the unit is available for showings during or after the turnover work.

faqs.q: Can one request cover several units?
faqs.a: Yes. Requests from self-managing landlords and property managers are welcome for single units and for several properties. Share your locations and the turnover work you send out most so visits are planned well.

faqs.q: Do the photos help with my move-in records?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask for before-and-after photos of completed items. Use them in your listing and keep them with your move-in condition record, alongside the walk-through you do with the new tenant.

faqs.q: Which areas are covered?
faqs.a: Requests come from Collingwood, Wasaga Beach, Stayner, Barrie and nearby communities. Include the address when you request a quote, and the service provider can confirm coverage.
